title: Business-as-Code
text:
1 Summary
We’re beginning to come to grips with how Large Language Models (LLMs) will impact the labor market. What does it mean to be a knowledge-worker when there exists a omni-present, intelligent, efficient robotic knowledge-worker which costs $20 per month?
The primary limitations seem to be:

The managerial capacity required to safely and reliably oversee the content which an LLM produces.
What is the price for which a customer is willing to pay for LLM generated content in the market in which an LLM is deployed?

Problem #1 is an engineering problem, most efficiently solved by the creators of the LLMs released for our use. While there is an immense creativity required to design a solution which fulfills the safety, efficiency, and resource requirements of any profitable organization- for me to write about engineering solutions would be the wrong side of comical.
Problem #2, on the other hand, I can write something semi-interesting about.
